items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I have to add that Ella Fitzgerald was on that bill with us, and above the plaque that I just mentioned, there was a picture sent from President Ford, and was taken of he and his wife, Betty, with the Lawson-Haggard band

ctx.x: broke up, until they broke away from Richard Gibson, he sold the band to an agent in Arizona, and his name -- he still is the bassist for the World's Greatest Jazz Band, of Yank Lawson and Bob Haggard. His name is Bark Hickox, and anybody who'd ever like to hear the World's Greatest Jazz Band in person -- we're open for engagements. His address is 4350 East Camelback Road, Phoenix, Arizona 85108.

Among other credits in the World's Greatest Jazz Band, and one of the things that I am most proud of, I just went in my living room and brought back a plaque, and the plaque was sent from the White House in Washington, D.C. I must read what it says: It says, "Dear Mr. Leeman, Mrs. Ford and I were delighted that our guests had such an enjoyable evening in the White House Rose Garden, on July 20th. A Salute To American Music was certainly enthusiastically applauded by everyone present, and the World's Greatest Jazz…
That stemmed from a command performance. We were asked at the White House, and it was for a Centennial of American Music, which also pertains to these archives at the Rose Garden, 1976.
